proofUses.reason: Susceptibility-biased two-point upper bound under the stated convergence and spatial hypotheses.
Distant-point two-point upper bound under the stated convergence and spatial hypotheses.
A breadth-first tree of the short paths and one attached unrestricted path give a trivalent diagram with exactly one unrestricted factor; leaf summation cancels the susceptibility bias.

Fixed-radius intrinsic-ball moments are bounded lattice cylinder functions. For distant-point conditioning the short factors restrict every remaining diagram position to a finite deterministic ball, permitting the ratio limit.

Finite-triangle susceptibility and thinning give an explicit linear critical ball mean; the double-factorial moment bound yields an exponential tail and dyadic Borel–Cantelli upper volume control. FWHO supplies the distant-point ratio only where its hypotheses hold.

A bounded intrinsic exploration leaves independent exterior bonds. The finite explored mass vanishes after division by diverging susceptibility; distant-point conditioning instead uses a finite-position ratio bound.

The first small positive sphere in the outer half of an intrinsic ball bounds limiting mass by its size times the critical arm probability. Dyadic Borel–Cantelli and the existing upper tail give volume exponent two.
Average limiting sphere means over radii r to 2r, then split at a sphere-size threshold and optimize the boundary-density comparison.

Uniform subgraph arms bound the expected total number of extendible crossing bonds. Disjoint cutset energy bounds give the critical resistance tail; the history comparison transfers it to each admissible limit.
